children.text: Vvs_3

body.text: māhāyāne traidhātukaṃ vijñaptimātraṃ vyavasthāpyate | cittamātraṃ bho jinaputrā yad uta traidhātukam iti sūtrāt | cittaṃ mano vijñānaṃ vijñaptiś ceti paryāyāḥ | cittam atra sasaṃprayogam abhipretaṃ | matram ity arthapratiṣedhārthaṃ |
body.translated_text: In the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, the triple world is established as <s>vijñaptimātra</s> (consciousness-only). From the sūtra: "O sons of the Conqueror, the triple world is nothing but mind." <s>Citta</s> (mind), <s>manas</s> (mentation), <s>vijñāna</s> (cognition), and <s>vijñapti</s> (representation) are synonyms. "Mind" here is intended together with its associated mental factors. "Only" is for the purpose of denying external objects.

children.text:
vijñaptimātram evedam asadarthāvabhāsanāt |
yadvat taimirikasyāsat keśoṇḍukādidarśanaṃ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: This is nothing but <s>vijñapti</s> (representation), since unreal objects appear — just as for one with an eye-disease, there is perception of unreal hairs, spots, and the like. (verse 1)

body.text: atra codyate | kaścid artho nāsti /
body.translated_text: Here the objection is raised: if there is no object whatsoever,

children.text:
na deśakālaniyamaḥ saṃtānāniyamo na ca |
na ca kṛtyakriyā yuktā vijñaptir yadi nārthataḥ || 2 ||
children.translated_text: then the restriction of place and time, the non-restriction to a single mental continuum, and the functional efficacy of action are not established, if <s>vijñapti</s> (representation) does not arise from objects. (verse 2)

body.text: kim uktaṃ bhavati | yadi vinā rūpādyarthena rūpādivijñaptir utpadyate na rūpādyarthāt | kasmāt kvacid deśa utpadyate na sarvatra | tatraiva ca deśe kadācid utpadyate na sarvadā | taddeśakālapratiṣṭhitānāṃ sarveṣāṃ saṃtānāniyama utpadyate na kevalam ekasya | yathā taimirikāṇāṃ saṃtāne keśādyābhāso nānyeṣāṃ | kasmād yat taimirikaiḥ keśabhramarādi dṛśyate tena keśādikriyā na kriyate na ca tad anyair na kriyate | yad annapānavastraviṣāyudhādi svapne dṛśyate tenānnādikriyā na kriyate na ca tad anyair na kriyate | gandharvanagareṇāsattvān nagarakriyā na kriyate na ca tad anyair na kriyate | tasmād asadabhāvāvabhāsane deśakālaniyamaḥ saṃtānāniyamaḥ kṛtyakriyā ca na yujyate | na khalu na yujyate | yasmāt |
body.translated_text: What is being said? If representation of form and so forth arises without objects such as form, and not from objects such as form — why does it arise only in a certain place and not everywhere? And in that very place, why does it arise only sometimes and not always? Why does it arise in the mental continua of all those situated in that place and time, and not in just one person's alone — just as the appearance of hairs and such occurs in the continua of those with eye-disease and not in others? Why is it that the hairs, bees, and such seen by those with eye-disease do not perform the function of hairs and so forth, whereas those seen by others do? Why is it that the food, drink, clothing, poison, weapons, and such seen in a dream do not perform the function of food and so forth, whereas those seen by others do? Why is it that a <s>gandharva</s>-city, being unreal, does not perform the function of a city, whereas those seen by others do? Therefore, when unreal things appear, the restriction of place and time, the non-restriction to a single continuum, and functional efficacy are not established. This is certainly not so, because:

children.text: deśādiniyamaḥ siddhaḥ svapnavat
children.translated_text: The restriction of place and so forth is established, as in a dream.

body.text: svapna iva svapnavat | kathaṃ tāvat | svapne vināpy arthena kvacid eva deśe kiṃcid bhramarārāmastrīpurūṣādikaṃ dṛśyate na sarvatra | tatraiva ca deśe kadācid dṛśyate na sarvakālam iti siddho vināpy arthena deśakālaniyamaḥ |
body.translated_text: "As in a dream" means like a dream. How so, to begin with? In a dream, even without any real object, something such as bees, gardens, women, men, and the like is seen only in a certain place and not everywhere. And in that very place, it is seen only sometimes and not at all times. Thus, even without real objects, the restriction of place and time is established.

children.text:
pretavat punaḥ |
saṃtānāniyamaḥ
children.translated_text: Furthermore, as in the case of hungry ghosts, the non-restriction to a single continuum

children.text: Vvs_4

body.text: siddha iti vartate | pretānām iva pretavat | kathaṃ siddhaḥ samaṃ |
body.translated_text: is established — this is to be supplied. "As in the case of hungry ghosts" means like hungry ghosts. How is it established? Equally,

body.text: sarvaiḥ pūyanadyādidarśane || 3 ||
body.translated_text: in the seeing of rivers of pus and such by all of them. (verse 3)

body.text: pūyapūrṇā nadī pūyanadī | ghṛtaghaṭavat | tulyakarmavipākāvasthā hi pretāḥ sarve 'pi pūyapūrṇāṃ nadīṃ paśyanti naika eva | yathā pūyapūrṇām evaṃ mūtrapurīṣādipūrṇāṃ daṇḍāsidharaiś ca puruṣair adhiṣṭhitām ity ādigrahaṇena | evaṃ saṃtānāniyamo vijñaptinām asaty apy arthe siddhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: A river full of pus is a "pus-river" — like "a pot of ghee." For all hungry ghosts, being in the same state of karmic fruition, see a river full of pus — not just a single one. Just as they see it full of pus, so too full of urine, excrement, and such, and guarded by men bearing staves and swords — this is indicated by the word "and such." Thus the non-restriction of representations to a single continuum is established even when objects do not exist.

children.text: svapnopaghātavat kṛtyakriyā
children.translated_text: Functional efficacy is established as in the case of dream-harm,

body.text: siddha iti veditavyaṃ | yathā svapne dvayasamāpattim antareṇa śukravisargalakṣaṇaḥ svapnopaghātaḥ | evaṃ tāvad anyānyair dṛṣṭāntair deśakālaniyamādicatuṣṭayaṃ siddhaṃ |
body.translated_text: as should be understood. Just as in a dream, without the union of two, there occurs dream-harm characterized by the emission of semen. Thus, by these various examples, all four — the restriction of place and time, and so forth — are established.

children.text:
narakavat punaḥ |
sarvaṃ
children.translated_text: Furthermore, as in the case of hells, everything

body.text: siddham iti veditavyaṃ | narakeṣv iva narakavat | kathaṃ siddhaṃ |
body.translated_text: is established — as should be understood. "As in the case of hells" means like in the hells. How is it established?

body.text: narakapālādidarśane taiś ca bādhane || 4 ||
body.translated_text: In the seeing of hell-guardians and such, and in the torment caused by them. (verse 4)

body.text: yathā hi narakeṣu nārakāṇāṃ narakapālādidarśanaṃ deśakālaniyamena siddhaṃ | śvavāyasāyasaparvatādyāgamanagamanadarśanaṃ cety ādigrahaṇena | sarveṣāṃ ca naikasyaiva taiś ca tadbādhanaṃ siddham asatsv api narakapālādiṣu samānasvakarmavipākādhipatyāt | tathānyatrāpi sarvam etad deśakālaniyamādicatuṣtayaṃ siddham iti veditavyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: For in the hells, the seeing of hell-guardians and such by hell-beings is established with restriction of place and time. And the seeing of the coming and going of dogs, crows, iron mountains, and such — this is indicated by "and such." And the torment caused by them to all beings and not to just one alone is established, even though the hell-guardians and such do not truly exist, due to the predominant influence of their common karmic fruition. Likewise, in other cases too, all four — the restriction of place and time, and so forth — should be understood as established.

body.text: kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇaṃ narakapālās te ca śvāno vāyasāś ca sattvā neṣyante | ayogāt | na hi te nārakā yujyante | tathaiva tadduḥkhāpratisaṃvedanāt | parasparaṃ yātayatām ime nārakā ime narakapālā iti vyavasthā na syāt | tulyākṛtipramāṇabalānāṃ ca parasparaṃ yātayatāṃ na tathā bhayaṃ syāt | dāhaduḥkhaṃ ca pradīptāyām ayomayyāṃ bhūmāv asahamānāḥ kathaṃ tatra parān yātayeyuḥ | anārakāṇāṃ vā narake kutaḥ saṃbhavaḥ | kathaṃ tāvat tiraścāṃ svargasaṃbhavaḥ | evaṃ narakeṣu tiryakpretaviśeṣāṇāṃ narakapālādīnāṃ saṃbhavaḥ syāt |
body.translated_text: What then is the reason why the hell-guardians (<s>narakapāla</s>) and those dogs and crows are not accepted as [real] sentient beings? Because of inconsistency (<s>ayoga</s>). For they cannot be hell-beings (<s>nāraka</s>), since they likewise do not experience that suffering. When they mutually torment each other, the distinction 'these are hell-beings, these are hell-guardians' would not hold. And when those of equal form, size, and strength torment each other, there would not be such fear. And those unable to bear the burning suffering on the blazing iron ground — how could they torment others there? Or, for non-hell-beings, how could there be birth in hell? How, to begin with, could there be the birth of animals in heaven? In the same way, there could be the birth of special types of animals and <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) such as hell-guardians and the like in the hells.

children.text:
tiraścāṃ saṃbhavaḥ svarge yathā na narake tathā |
na pretānāṃ yatas tajjaṃ duḥkhaṃ nānubhavanti te || 5 ||
children.translated_text: Just as there is birth of animals in heaven, so [there should] not [be] in hell; not of <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), because they do not experience the suffering born of that [realm]. || 5 ||

body.text: ye hi tiryañcaḥ svarge saṃbhavanti te tadbhājanalokasukhasaṃvartanīyena karmaṇā tatra saṃbhūtās tajjaṃ sukhaṃ pratyanubhavanti | na caiva narakapālādayo nārakaṃ duḥkhaṃ pratyanubhavanti | tasmān na tiraścāṃ saṃbhavo yukto nāpi pretānāṃ ||
body.translated_text: For those animals that are born in heaven are born there by <s>karma</s> that ripens into the happiness of that vessel-world (<s>bhājanaloka</s>), and they experience the happiness born of that. But the hell-guardians and others do not experience hellish suffering. Therefore the birth of animals there is not appropriate, nor that of <s>pretas</s>.

body.text: teṣāṃ tarhi (

children.text: Vvs_5

) nārakāṇāṃ karmabhis tatra bhūtaviśeṣāḥ saṃbhavanti varṇākṛtipramāṇabalaviśiṣṭā ye narakapālādisaṃjñāṃ pratilabhante | tathā ca pariṇamanti | yad dvidhāṃ hastavikṣepādikriyāṃ kurvanto dṛśyante bhayotpādanārthaṃ | yathā meṣākṛtayaḥ parvatā āgacchanto gacchanto 'yaḥśālmalīvane ca kaṇṭakā adhomukhībhavanta ūrddhvamukhībhavantaś ceti | na te na saṃbhavanty eva |
children.translated_text: by the <s>karmas</s> of those hell-beings, special elemental beings (<s>bhūtaviśeṣa</s>) arise there, distinguished by color, form, size, and strength, who receive the designation 'hell-guardians' and the like. And they transform accordingly — such that they are seen performing twofold actions like hand-striking and so forth, for the purpose of generating fear. Just as the mountains in the form of rams are seen coming and going, and in the iron <s>śālmalī</s>-tree forest the thorns face downward and face upward. It is not that they do not arise at all.

body.translated_text: Of those, then,

children.text:
yadi tatkarmabhis tatra bhūtānāṃ saṃbhavas tathā |
iṣyate pariṇāmaś ca kiṃ vijñānasya neṣyate || 6 ||
children.translated_text: If by their <s>karmas</s> the birth of elemental beings there in such a manner is accepted, and [their] transformation too, why is [the transformation] of consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) not accepted? || 6 ||

body.text: vijñānasyaiva tatkarmabhis tathā pariṇāmaḥ kasmān neṣyate kiṃ punar bhūtāni kalpyante ||
body.translated_text: Why is it not accepted that consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) itself transforms in such a way by those <s>karmas</s>? Why then are material elements (<s>bhūta</s>) additionally postulated?

body.text: api ca |
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text:
karmaṇo vāsanānyatra phalam anyatra kalpyate |
tatraiva neṣyate yatra vāsanā kiṃ nu kāraṇaṃ || 7 ||
children.translated_text: The imprint (<s>vāsanā</s>) of <s>karma</s> is in one place; the fruit is postulated in another. That it is not accepted right there where the imprint is — what is the reason? || 7 ||

body.text: yena hi karmaṇā nārakāṇāṃ tatra tādṛśo bhūtānāṃ saṃbhavaḥ kalpyate pariṇāmaś ca tasya karmaṇo vāsanā teṣāṃ vijñānasaṃtānasaṃniviṣṭā nānyatra | yatraiva ca vāsanā tatraiva tasyāḥ phalaṃ tādṛśo vijñānapariṇāmaḥ kiṃ neṣyate | yatra vāsanā nāsti tatra tasyāḥ phalaṃ kalpyata iti kim atra kāraṇaṃ ||
body.translated_text: For whatever <s>karma</s> by which such a birth and transformation of elemental beings is postulated for the hell-beings — the imprint (<s>vāsanā</s>) of that <s>karma</s> is deposited in their own stream of consciousness (<s>vijñānasaṃtāna</s>), not elsewhere. And the fruit of that imprint right there where the imprint is — namely, such a transformation of consciousness (<s>vijñānapariṇāma</s>) — why is it not accepted? That the fruit of the imprint is postulated where there is no imprint — what is the reason for this?

body.text: āgamaḥ kāraṇaṃ | yadi vijñānam eva rūpādipratibhāsaṃ syān na rūpādiko 'rthas tadā rūpādyāyatanāstitvaṃ bhagavatā noktaṃ syāt | akāraṇam etad yasmāt |
body.translated_text: Scripture (<s>āgama</s>) is the reason. If consciousness alone appeared as form and the rest, and there were no object such as form and the rest, then the <s>Bhagavān</s> would not have declared the existence of the sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>) of form and the rest. This is no [valid] reason, because:

children.text:
rūpādyāyatanāstitvaṃ tadvineyajanaṃ prati |
abhiprāyavaśād uktam upapādukasattvavat || 8 ||
children.translated_text: The existence of the sense-bases of form and the rest was stated with a special intention (<s>abhiprāya</s>), directed toward beings to be instructed thereby — just like [his statement about] spontaneously born (<s>upapāduka</s>) beings. || 8 ||

body.text: yathāsti sattva upapāduka ity uktaṃ bhagavatā abhiprāyavaśāc cittasaṃtatyanucchedam āyatyām abhipretya |
body.translated_text: Just as 'there is a spontaneously born being' was said by the <s>Bhagavān</s> with a special intention, having in mind the non-interruption of the stream of consciousness (<s>cittasaṃtāna</s>) in the future,

children.text: nāstīha sattva ātmā vā dharmās tv ete sahetukāḥ
children.translated_text: 'There is no being here, no self; but these are <s>dharmas</s> with causes'

body.text: iti vacanāt | evaṃ rūpādyāyatanāstitvam apy uktaṃ bhagavatā taddeśanāvineyajanam adhikṛtyety ābhiprāyikaṃ tad vacanaṃ ||
body.translated_text: — because of this statement. In the same way, the existence of the sense-bases of form and the rest was also stated by the <s>Bhagavān</s> with reference to beings who are to be instructed by that teaching — thus that statement is intentional (<s>ābhiprāyika</s>).

body.text: ko 'tra abhiprāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: What is the intention here?

children.text:
yataḥ svabījād vijñaptir yadābhāsā pravartate |
dvividhāyatanatvena te tasyā munir abravīt || 9 ||
children.translated_text: Since from its own seed (<s>svabīja</s>), cognition (<s>vijñapti</s>) arises appearing as whatever [object], the <s>Muni</s> (Sage) declared those two as the [respective] sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>) of that [cognition]. || 9 ||

body.text: kim uktaṃ bhavati | rūpapratibhāsā vijñaptir yataḥ svabījāt pariṇāmaviśeṣaprāptād utpadyate tac ca bījaṃ yat pratibhāsā ca sā te tasyā vijñapteś cakṣūrūpāyatanatvena (

children.text: Vvs_6

) yathākramaṃ bhagavān abravīt | evaṃ yāvat spraṣṭavyapratibhāsā vijñaptir yataḥ svabījāt pariṇāmaviśeṣaprāptād utpadyate tac ca bījaṃ yat pratibhāsā ca sā te tasyā kāyaspraṣṭavyāyatanatvena yathākranaṃ bhagavān abravīd ity ayam abhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, up to: the cognition appearing as tangible objects (<s>spraṣṭavya</s>) arises from its own seed that has reached a specific transformation — and that seed, and that appearance — those are declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> as the body and tangible-object sense-bases (<s>kāyaspraṣṭavyāyatana</s>) of that cognition, respectively — this is the intention.

body.translated_text: What is being said? The cognition (<s>vijñapti</s>) appearing as form arises from its own seed that has reached a specific transformation (<s>pariṇāmaviśeṣa</s>) — and that seed, and that appearance — those are declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> as the eye sense-base and the form sense-base (<s>cakṣūrūpāyatana</s>) of that cognition, respectively.

body.text: evaṃ punar abhiprāyavaśena deśayitvā ko guṇāḥ |
body.translated_text: Having thus taught by way of special intention, what are the merits [of doing so]?

children.text: tathā pudgalanairātmyapraveśo hi
children.translated_text: For thus [there is] entry into the selflessness of the person (<s>pudgalanairātmya</s>)

body.text: tathā hi deśyamāne pudgalanairātmyaṃ praviśanti | dvayād vijñānaṣaṭkaṃ pravartate | na tu kaścid eko draṣṭāsti na yāvan mantety evaṃ viditvā ye pudgalanairātmyadeśanāvineyās te pudgalanairātmyaṃ praviśanti |
body.translated_text: For indeed, when [the teaching] is being given, they enter [the understanding of] the selflessness of persons (<s>pudgalanairātmya</s>). From the dyad [of sense-faculty and object], the six kinds of consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) arise. But there is no single seer, nor anyone who thinks — having understood thus, those who are to be trained by the teaching of the selflessness of persons enter [the understanding of] the selflessness of persons.

children.text:
anyathā punaḥ |
deśanā dharmanairātmyapraveśaḥ
children.translated_text: In another way, however, the teaching [leads to] entry into the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>).

body.text: anyatheti vijñaptimātradeśanā | kathaṃ dharmanairātmyapraveśaḥ | vijñaptimātram idaṃ rūpādidharmapratibhāsam utpadyate na tu rūpādilakṣaṇo dharmaḥ ko 'py astīti viditvā | yadi tarhi sarvathā dharmo nāsti tad api vijñaptimātraṃ nāstīti kathaṃ tarhi vyavasthāpyate | na khalu sarvathā dharmo nāstīty evaṃ dharmanairātmyapraveśo bhavati | api tu |
body.translated_text: 'In another way' refers to the teaching of consciousness-only (<s>vijñaptimātra</s>). How does entry into the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> [occur]? By understanding that this [experience], having the appearance of <s>dharmas</s> such as form (<s>rūpa</s>) etc., arises as consciousness-only (<s>vijñaptimātra</s>), and that no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever with the characteristics of form etc. exists. [Objection:] If <s>dharmas</s> do not exist at all, then consciousness-only too does not exist — how then can it be established? [Reply:] Entry into the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> does not occur by [establishing] that <s>dharmas</s> do not exist at all. Rather,

body.text: kalpitātmanā || 10 ||
body.translated_text: [Their selflessness is] by the imagined self (<s>kalpitātman</s>). || 10 ||

body.text: yo bālair dharmāṇāṃ svabhāvo grāhyagrāhakādiḥ parikalpatas tena kalpitenātmanā teṣāṃ nairātmyaṃ na tv anabhilāpyenātmanā yo buddhānāṃ viṣaya iti | evaṃ vijñaptimātrasyāpi vijñaptyantaraparikalpitenātmanā nairātmyapraveśāt vijñaptimātravyavasthāpanayā sarvadharmāṇāṃ nairātmyapraveśo bhavati na tu tadastitvāpavādāt | itarathā hi vijñapter api vijñaptyantaram arthaḥ syād iti vijñaptimātratvaṃ na sidhyetārthavatītvād vijñaptīnāṃ ||
body.translated_text: The essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of <s>dharmas</s> that is imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>) by the childish — such as [the duality of] apprehended and apprehender (<s>grāhyagrāhaka</s>) — by that imagined self, [there is] their selflessness; but not by the inexpressible (<s>anabhilāpya</s>) self that is the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>. Thus, since entry into selflessness [occurs] through the self that is imagined by another consciousness (<s>vijñaptyantara</s>), through the establishment of consciousness-only, there is entry into the selflessness of all <s>dharmas</s> — but not by denying their existence. For otherwise, consciousness too would have another consciousness as its object, and the thesis of consciousness-only-ness (<s>vijñaptimātratva</s>) would not be established, since cognitions would [then] have [external] objects.

body.text: kathaṃ punar idaṃ pratyetavyam anenābhiprāyeṇa bhagavatā rūpādyāyatanāstitvam uktaṃ na punaḥ santy eva tāni yāni rūpādivijñaptīnāṃ pratyekaṃ viṣayībhavanti iti | yasmāt |
body.translated_text: But how is it to be understood that the Blessed One spoke of the existence of sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>) such as form etc. with this intention, and not [meaning] that those [forms etc.] really exist as objects perceived individually by the cognitions of form etc.? Because:

children.text:
na tad ekaṃ na cānekaṃ viṣayaḥ paramāṇuśaḥ |
na ca te saṃhatā yasmāt paramāṇur na sidhyati || 11 ||
children.translated_text: That [external object] is not one, nor is it many as atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>); nor are those [atoms] aggregated — because the atom is not established. || 11 ||

body.text: iti | kim uktaṃ bhavati | yat tadrūpādikam āyatanaṃ rūpādivijñaptīnāṃ pratyekaṃ viṣayaḥ syāt tad ekaṃ vā syād yathāvayavirūpaṃ kalpyate vaiśeṣikaiḥ | anekaṃ vā paramāṇuśaḥ | saṃhatā vā ta eva paramāṇavaḥ | na tāvad ekaṃ viṣayo bhavaty avayavebhyo 'nyasyāvayavirūpasya kvacid apy agrahaṇāt | nāpy anekaṃ paramāṇūnāṃ (

children.text: Vvs_7
children.translated_text: (Vvs 7)

children.text: ) pratyekam agrahaṇāt | nāpi te saṃhatā viṣayībhavanti | yasmāt paramāṇur ekaṃ dravyaṃ na sidhyati ||
children.translated_text: ) are not individually apprehended. Nor do they become objects as aggregates, because the atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>) as a single substance (<s>dravya</s>) is not established.

body.translated_text: What is being said? If that sense-base of form etc. were the individual object of the cognitions of form etc., it would be either one — as the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> conceive the whole (<s>avayavirūpa</s>) — or many, as atoms; or those very atoms aggregated. First, the object is not one, since the whole, as something different from its parts (<s>avayava</s>), is never apprehended anywhere. Nor is it many, since the atoms individually (

body.text: kathaṃ na sidhyati | yasmāt |
body.translated_text: How is it not established? Because:

body.text: ṣaṭkena yugapad yogāt paramāṇoḥ ṣaḍaṃśatā |
body.translated_text: Due to simultaneous conjunction with six [other atoms], the atom would have six parts (<s>ṣaḍaṃśatā</s>);

body.text: ṣaḍbhyo digbhyaḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ paramāṇubhir yugapad yoge sati paramāṇoḥ ṣaḍaṃśatā prāpnoti | ekasya yo deśas tatrānyasyāsaṃbhavāt |
body.translated_text: When there is simultaneous conjunction with six atoms from the six directions, the atom would acquire six parts — because in the place occupied by one [atom], another cannot exist.

children.text:
ṣaṇṇāṃ samānadeśatvāt piṇḍaḥ syād
aṇumātrakaḥ || 12 ||
children.translated_text: If the six [atoms] occupy the same place, the aggregate (<s>piṇḍa</s>) would be merely atom-sized. || 12 ||

body.text: atha ya evaikasya paramāṇor deśaḥ sa eva ṣaṇṇāṃ | tena sarveṣāṃ samānadeśatvāt sarvaḥ piṇḍaḥ paramāṇumātraḥ syāt parasparāvyatirekād iti na kaścit piṇḍo dṛśyaḥ syāt ||
body.translated_text: But if the place of one atom is the same as that of the six, then since all [atoms] would occupy the same place, every aggregate would be merely atom-sized — since they would be mutually non-distinct — and thus no aggregate would be visible.

body.text: naiva hi paramāṇavaḥ saṃyujyante niravayavatvāt | mā bhūd eṣa doṣaprasaṅgaḥ | saṃhatās tu parasparaṃ saṃyujyanta iti kāśmīravaibhāṣikās ta idaṃ praṣṭavyāḥ | yaḥ paramāṇūnāṃ saṃghāto na sa tebhyo 'rthāntaram iti |
body.translated_text: Indeed, atoms do not conjoin, because they are partless (<s>niravayava</s>). [Objection by the <s>Kāśmīra Vaibhāṣikas</s>:] Let this fault not arise — aggregates (<s>saṃhata</s>) conjoin with one another. They should be asked this: The aggregate of atoms is not something different from them —

body.text: paramāṇor asaṃyogāt tatsaṃghāte 'sti kasya saḥ |
body.translated_text: Since the atom has no conjunction, to what in their aggregate does

body.text: saṃyoga iti vartate |
body.translated_text: conjunction belong? [The word 'conjunction' is to be supplied.]

body.text: na cānavayavatvena tatsaṃyogo na sidhyati || 13 ||
body.translated_text: And [one cannot say that] because of partlessness, their conjunction is not established [for that reason alone]. || 13 ||

body.text: atha saṃghātā apy anyonyaṃ na saṃyujyante | na tarhi paramāṇūnāṃ niravayavatvāt saṃyogo na sidhyatīti vaktavyaṃ | sāvayavasyāpi hi saṃghātasya saṃyogānabhyupagamāt | tasmāt paramāṇur ekaṃ dravyaṃ na sidhyati | yadi ca paramāṇoḥ saṃyoga iṣyate yadi vā neṣyate |
body.translated_text: If aggregates too do not conjoin with one another, then one should not say that the conjunction of atoms is not established merely because they are partless — since conjunction is not accepted even for the aggregate, which has parts (<s>sāvayava</s>). Therefore, the atom as a single substance is not established. Whether conjunction of the atom is accepted or not:

body.text: digbhāgabhedī yasyāsti tasyaikatvaṃ na yujyate |
body.translated_text: That which has differentiation of directional parts (<s>digbhāgabheda</s>) — its unity is not tenable.

body.text: anyo hi paramāṇoḥ pūrvadigbhāgo yāvad adhodigbhāga iti digbhāgabhede sati kathaṃ tadātmakasya paramāṇor ekatvaṃ yokṣyate |
body.translated_text: For the eastern directional part of the atom is different from [its parts in other directions] up to the lower directional part — when there is such differentiation of directional parts, how can the unity of the atom, whose nature is constituted by these [parts], be maintained?

children.text: chāyāvṛtī katha vā
children.translated_text: And how [can] shadow and obstruction —

body.text: yady ekaikasya paramāṇor digbhāgabhedo na syād ādityodaye katham anyatra chāyā bhavaty anyatrātapaḥ | na hi tasyānyaḥ pradeśo 'sti yatrātapo na syāt | āvaraṇaṃ ca kathaṃ bhavati paramāṇoḥ paramāṇvantareṇa yadi digbhāgabhedo neṣyate | na hi kaścid api paramāṇoḥ parabhāgo 'sti yatrāgamanād anyenānyasya pratighātaḥ syāt | asati ca pratighāte sarveṣāṃ samānadeśatvāt sarvaḥ saṃghātaḥ (

children.text: Vvs_8
children.translated_text: [Vvs 8]

children.text: ) paramāṇumātraḥ syād ity uktaṃ | kim evaṃ neṣyate piṇḍasya te chāyāvṛtī na paramāṇor iti | kiṃ khalu paramāṇubhyo 'nyaḥ piṇḍa iṣyate yasya te syātāṃ | nety āha |
children.translated_text: would be the size of a single atom — thus it has been stated. [Objection:] Why is it not accepted that shadow and obstruction belong to the aggregate (<s>piṇḍa</s>), not to the atom? [Reply:] Is the aggregate, then, accepted as something other than the atoms, to which those [properties] would belong? [The opponent] says: No.

body.translated_text: If there is no differentiation of directional parts for each individual <s>paramāṇu</s> (atom), then when the sun rises, how is there shadow in one place and sunlight in another? For there is no other part of it where there would not be sunlight. And how can there be obstruction (<s>āvaraṇa</s>) of one atom by another atom, if differentiation of directional parts is not accepted? For there is no farther side of the atom whatsoever, by arriving at which one [atom] would obstruct another. And in the absence of mutual obstruction, since all [atoms] would occupy the same location, every aggregate

body.text: anyo na piṇḍaś cen na tasya te || 14 ||
body.translated_text: If the aggregate is not something other [than the atoms], then those [properties] do not belong to it. || 14 ||

body.text: yadi nānyaḥ paramāṇubhyaḥ piṇḍa iṣyate na te tasyeti siddhaṃ bhavati | saṃniveśaparikalpa eṣaḥ paramāṇuḥ saṃghāta iti vā ||
body.translated_text: If the aggregate is not accepted as something other than the atoms, it is established that those [properties — shadow and obstruction —] do not belong to it. This is merely a conceptual construction of arrangement (<s>saṃniveśaparikalpa</s>) — 'this is an atom' or 'this is an aggregate.'

body.text: kim anayā cintayā lakṣaṇaṃ / tu rūpādi yadi na pratiṣidhyate | kiṃ punas teṣāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ | cakṣurādiviṣayatvaṃ nīlāditvaṃ ca | tad evedaṃ saṃpradhāryate | yat tac cakṣurādīnāṃ viṣayo nīlapītādikam iṣyate kiṃ tad ekaṃ dravyam atha vā tad anekam iti | kiṃ cātaḥ | anekatve doṣa uktaṃ |
body.translated_text: What is the use of this inquiry? But if the characteristic of form (<s>rūpa</s>) and the rest is not denied, [what is the problem?] What, then, is their characteristic? Being an object of the eye and the other [sense faculties], and being blue and so forth. This very point is now to be carefully considered: that which is accepted as the object of the eye and the other [senses] — blue, yellow, and so forth — is it a single substance (<s>dravya</s>), or is it manifold? And what follows from this? The fault in [accepting it as] manifold has been stated.

children.text:
ekatve na krameṇetir yugapan na grahāgrahau |
vicchinnānekavṛttiś ca sūkṣmānīkṣā ca no bhavet || 15 ||
children.translated_text: If [it is] one, there would be no traversing in sequence; no simultaneous apprehension and non-apprehension; no separate, manifold occurrences; and no non-perception of the subtle. || 15 ||

body.text: yadi yāvad vicchinnaṃ nānekaṃ cakṣuṣo viṣayas tad ekaṃ dravyaṃ kalpyate pṛthivyāṃ krameṇetir na syād gamanam ity arthaḥ | sakṛtpādakṣepeṇa sarvasya gatatvāt | arvāgbhāgasya ca grahaṇaṃ parabhāgasya cāgrahaṇaṃ yugapan na syāt | na hi tasyaiva tadānīṃ grahaṇaṃ cāgrahaṇaṃ ca yuktam | vicchinnasya cānekasya hastyaśvādikasyaikatra vṛttir na syād yatraiva hy ekaṃ tatraivāparam iti kathaṃ tayor viccheda iṣyate | kathaṃ vā tad ekaṃ yat prāptaṃ ca tābhyāṃ na ca prāptam antarāle tac chūnyagrahaṇāt | sūkṣmāṇāṃ caudakajantūnāṃ sthūlaiḥ samānarūpāṇām anīkṣaṇaṃ na syād | yadi lakṣaṇabhedād eva dravyāntaratvaṃ kalpyate nānyathā | tasmād avaśyaṃ paramāṇuśo bhedaḥ kalpayitavyaḥ | sa caiko na sidhyati | tasyāsiddhau rūpādīnāṃ cakṣurādiviṣayatvam asiddham iti siddhaṃ vijñaptimātraṃ bhavatīti ||
body.translated_text: If as much as is distinct is not manifold, and the object of the eye is conceived as a single substance — then on earth there would be no traversing in sequence — the meaning is: no going [from place to place] — since the entire [earth] would be traversed by a single step. And there would be no simultaneous apprehension of the near side and non-apprehension of the far side, for it is not reasonable that there be both apprehension and non-apprehension of the very same [thing] at the same time. And there would be no occurrence of separate, manifold [things] such as elephants, horses, and so forth in a single place — for where one is, there too is the other, and so how can their separateness be maintained? And how can it be one [substance], which is both occupied by them and not occupied [by them] in the interval, since that empty interval is apprehended? And there would be no non-perception of subtle aquatic creatures that are of the same visible form as the coarser [medium]. If distinctness of substance is conceived solely on the basis of distinction of characteristics, and not otherwise — then necessarily a division atom by atom must be conceived. And that single [atom] is not established. When that is not established, the being-objects-of-the-eye-and-other-[senses] of form (<s>rūpa</s>) and the rest is not established — thus it is established that there is <s>vijñaptimātra</s> (consciousness-only).

body.text: pramāṇavaśād astitvaṃ nāstitvaṃ vā nirdhāryate sarveṣāṃ ca pramāṇānāṃ pratyakṣaṃ pramāṇaṃ gariṣṭam ity asaty arthe katham iyaṃ buddhir bhavati pratyakṣam iti |
body.translated_text: By the force of the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), either the existence or non-existence [of things] is determined. And among all means of valid knowledge, direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) is the most authoritative. If there is no [external] object, how does this cognition arise: 'This is direct perception'?

children.text: pratyakṣabuddhiḥ svapnādau yathā
children.translated_text: The cognition of direct perception in dreams and the like [arises]

body.text: vināpy artheneti pūrvam eva jñāpitaṃ
body.translated_text: even without an [external] object — this has already been shown [above].

children.text:
sā ca yadā tadā |
na so 'rtho dṛśyate tasya pratyakṣatvaṃ kathaṃ mataṃ || 16 ||
children.translated_text: And at the time when that [direct-perception cognition arises], that object is not seen. How, then, is its being direct perception maintained? || 16 ||

body.text: yadā ca sā pratyakṣabuddhir bhavatīdaṃ me pratyakṣam iti tadā na so 'rtho dṛśyate manovijñānenaiva paricchedāc cakṣurvijñānasya ca tadā niruddhatvād iti kathaṃ tasya pratyakṣatvam iṣṭaṃ | viśeṣeṇa tu kṣaṇikasya viṣayasya tadānīṃ (

children.text: Vvs_9
children.translated_text: [Vvs 9]

children.text: ) niruddham evaṃ tad rūpaṃ rasādikaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: that form (<s>rūpa</s>) or taste (<s>rasa</s>) and so forth has already ceased.

body.translated_text: And at the time when that cognition of direct perception arises — 'this is my direct perception' — that object is not seen, since it is determined only by the mental consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>), and since the visual consciousness (<s>cakṣurvijñāna</s>) has already ceased at that time. How, then, is its being direct perception accepted? Moreover, for a momentary (<s>kṣaṇika</s>) object, at that time

body.text: nānanubhūtaṃ manovijñānena smaryata ity avaśyam arthānubhavena bhavitavyaṃ tac ca darśanam ity evaṃ tadviṣayasya rūpādeḥ pratyakṣatvaṃ mataṃ | asiddham idam anubhūtasyārthasya smaraṇaṃ bhavatīti | yasmāt |
body.translated_text: [Objection:] What is not experienced (<s>ananubhūta</s>) is not remembered (<s>smaryate</s>) by the mental consciousness. Therefore there must have been an experience (<s>anubhava</s>) of the object, and that is perception (<s>darśana</s>) — thus the direct perceptuality of the object, form and the rest, is maintained. [Reply:] This is not established — that remembering occurs of an experienced object. Because:

children.text: uktaṃ yathā tadābhāsā vijñaptiḥ
children.translated_text: It has been stated that cognition (<s>vijñapti</s>) appears as that [object]

body.text: vināpy arthena yathārthābhāsā cakṣurvijñānādikā vijñaptir utpadyate tathoktaṃ |
body.translated_text: — even without an [external] object, it has been stated that visual consciousness and the rest arise with the appearance of an object. Thus,

body.text: smaraṇaṃ tataḥ |
body.translated_text: remembering [arises] from that [cognition itself].

body.text: tato hi vijñapteḥ smṛtisaṃprayuktā tatpratibhāsaiva rūpādivikalpikā manovijñaptir utpadyata iti na smṛtyutpādād arthānubhavaḥ sidhyati | yadi yathā svapne vijñaptir abhūtārthaviṣayā tathā jāgrato 'pi syāt tathaiva tadabhāvaṃ lokaḥ svayam avagacchet | na caivaṃ bhavati | tasmān na svapna ivārthopalabdhiḥ sarvā nirarthikā | idam ajñāpakaṃ | yasmāt |
body.translated_text: For from that <s>vijñapti</s> (representation) there arises a mental representation (<s>manovijñapti</s>) associated with memory, having the appearance of that [object], conceptualizing form and the like — therefore the arising of memory does not establish the experience of objects. If, just as in a dream <s>vijñapti</s> has an unreal object as its domain, so too in the waking state, then the world would itself understand the non-existence of that [object] in the same way. But this is not so. Therefore, not all apprehension of objects is objectless like a dream. This does not prove [the point], because:

body.text: svapnadṛgviṣayābhāvaṃ nāprabuddho 'vigacchati || 17 ||
body.translated_text: One who has not awakened does not understand the non-existence of dream-objects. (verse 17)

body.text: evaṃ vitathavikalpābhyāsavāsanānidrayā prasupto lokaḥ svapna ivābhūtam arthaṃ paśyan na prabuddhas tadabhāvaṃ yathāvan nāvagacchati | yadā tu tatpratipakṣalokottaranirvikalpajñānalābhāt prabuddho bhavati tadā tatpṛṣṭhalabdhaśuddhalaukikajñānasaṃmukhībhāvād viṣayābhāvaṃ yathāvad avagacchatīti samānam etat ||
body.translated_text: In this way, the world — asleep through the slumber of the habitual impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) from the practice of false conceptualization (<s>vitathavikalpa</s>) — seeing unreal objects as in a dream, not being awakened, does not understand their non-existence as it truly is. But when one becomes awakened through attaining the supramundane non-conceptual wisdom (<s>lokottaranirvikalpajñāna</s>) that is the antidote to that, then through the arising of the pure mundane knowledge (<s>śuddhalaukikajñāna</s>) obtained subsequently, one understands the non-existence of objects as it truly is — thus this [analogy] holds equally.

body.text: yadi svasaṃtānapariṇāmaviśeṣād eva satvānām arthapratibhāsā vijñaptaya utpadyante nārthaviśeṣāt | tadā ya eṣa pāpakalyāṇamitrasaṃparkāt sadasaddharmaśravaṇāc ca vijñaptiniyamaḥ sattvānāṃ sa kathaṃ sidhyati asati sadasatsaṃparke taddeśanāyāṃ ca |
body.translated_text: If representations with the appearance of objects arise for beings solely from a special transformation (<s>pariṇāmaviśeṣa</s>) of their own mental continua (<s>svasaṃtāna</s>) and not from any special object, then how is this regularity of <s>vijñapti</s> for beings — [arising] from association with bad and good friends, and from hearing true and false <s>Dharma</s> — established, when there is no real association with the good and bad, and no real teaching thereof?

body.text: anyonyādhipatitvena vijñaptiniyamo mithaḥ |
body.translated_text: The regularity of <s>vijñapti</s> is mutual, through the predominant influence (<s>ādhipatya</s>) of one another.

body.text: sarveṣāṃ hi sattvānām anyonyavijñaptyādhipatyena mitho vijñapter niyamo bhavati yathāyogaṃ | mitha iti parasparataḥ | ataḥ saṃtānāntaravijñaptiviśeṣāt saṃtānāntare vijñaptiviśeṣa utpadyate nārthaviśeṣāt | yadi yathā svapne nirarthikā vijñaptir evaṃ jāgrato 'pi syāt kasmāt kuśalākuśalasamudācāro suptāsuptayos tulyaṃ phalam iṣṭāniṣṭam āyatyāṃ na bhavati | yasmāt |
body.translated_text: For the regularity of <s>vijñapti</s> of all beings arises from the predominant influence of one another's <s>vijñapti</s>, as appropriate. 'Mutually' (<s>mithaḥ</s>) means reciprocally. Therefore, a special <s>vijñapti</s> arises in another's continuum from a special <s>vijñapti</s> in [yet] another's continuum — not from a special object. If, just as in a dream <s>vijñapti</s> is objectless, so too in the waking state, why does the fruit of wholesome and unwholesome conduct — desirable and undesirable — not become equal in the future for those who are asleep and those who are awake? Because:

body.text: middhenopahataṃ cittaṃ svapne tenāsamaṃ phalaṃ || 18 ||
body.translated_text: The mind is impaired by sleep (<s>middha</s>); therefore the fruit [of actions] in a dream is unequal. (verse 18)

body.text: idam atra kāraṇāṃ na tv arthasadbhāvaḥ ||
body.translated_text: This is the cause here, not the real existence of objects.

body.text: yadi vijñāptimātram evedaṃ na kasyacit kāyo 'sti na vāk ||
body.translated_text: If everything is <s>vijñaptimātra</s> (consciousness-only) and no one has a body or speech,

body.text: katham upakramyamāṇānām aurabhrikādibhir urabhrādīnāṃ (

children.text: Vvs_10
children.translated_text: [Reference: Vvs_10]

children.text: ) maraṇaṃ bhavti | atatkṛte vā tanmaraṇe katham aurabhrikādīnāṃ prāṇātipātāvadyena yogo bhavati |
children.translated_text: Or if their death is not caused by that [attack], how is there for butchers and such the fault (<s>avadya</s>) of taking life (<s>prāṇātipāta</s>)?

body.translated_text: how does the death of sheep and such occur when they are attacked by butchers and the like?

children.text:
maraṇam paravijñaptiviśeṣād vikriyā yathā |
smṛtilopādikānyeṣāṃ piśācādimanovaśāt || 19 ||
children.translated_text: Death [occurs] from a special transformation of another's <s>vijñapti</s>, just as the loss of memory and such [occur] in others from the mental power of <s>piśācas</s> (demons) and the like. (verse 19)

body.text: yathā hi piśācādimanovaśād anyeṣāṃ smṛtilopasvapnadarśanabhūtagrahāveśavikārā bhavanti | ṛddhivan manovaśāc ca | yathā sāraṇasyāryamahākātyāyanādhiṣṭhānāt svapnadarśanaṃ | āraṇyakarṣimanaḥpradoṣāc ca vemacitraparājayaḥ | tathā paravijñaptiviśeṣādhipatyāt pareṣāṃ jīvitendriyavirodhinī kācid vikriyotpadyate yayā sabhāgasaṃtativicchedākhyaṃ maraṇaṃ bhavatīti veditavyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: For just as from the mental power of <s>piśācas</s> and such, there occur in others loss of memory, dream-visions, possession by spirits (<s>bhūtagraha</s>), and [other] alterations. And from the mental power of one possessing supernatural ability (<s>ṛddhi</s>). Just as the dream-vision of <s>Sāraṇa</s> occurred from the supernatural determination (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) of the noble <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>. And the defeat of <s>Vemacitra</s> from the ill-will of a forest sage. Similarly, from the predominant influence of a special transformation of another's <s>vijñapti</s>, a certain transformation that is hostile to the life-faculty (<s>jīvitendriya</s>) arises in others, by which what is called the cutting-off of the similar-class continuum (<s>sabhāgasaṃtativiccheda</s>) — that is, death — occurs. This should be understood.

body.text: kathaṃ vā daṇḍakāraṇyaśūnyatvam ṛṣikopataḥ |
body.translated_text: How, then, [is there] the emptying of the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest from the anger of the sages?

body.text: yadi paravijñaptiviśeṣādhipatyāt sattvānāṃ maraṇaṃ neṣyate | manodaṇḍasya hi mahāsāvadyatvaṃ sādhayatā bhagavatopālir gṛhapatiḥ pṛṣṭaḥ | kaccit te gṛhapate śrutaṃ kena tāni daṇḍakāraṇyāni mātaṅgāraṇyāni kaliṅgāraṇyāni śūnyāni medhyībhūtāni | tenoktaṃ | śrutaṃ me bho gautama ṛṣīṇāṃ manaḥpradoṣeṇeti |
body.translated_text: If the death of beings from the predominant influence of a special transformation of another's <s>vijñapti</s> is not accepted — for the <s>Bhagavān</s>, in establishing that the mind-punishment (<s>manodaṇḍa</s>) is greatly faulty, questioned the householder <s>Upāli</s>: 'Have you, householder, heard by whom those <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forests, <s>Mātaṅga</s> forests, <s>Kaliṅga</s> forests were made empty and desolate?' He replied: 'I have heard, O <s>Gautama</s>, by the ill-will of the sages.'

body.text: manodaṇḍo mahāvadyaḥ kathaṃ vā tena sidhyati || 20 ||
body.translated_text: How, then, is the great fault of the mind-punishment (<s>manodaṇḍa</s>) established by that? (verse 20)

body.text: yady evaṃ kalpyate | tadabhiprasannair amānuṣais tadvāsinaḥ sattvā utsāditā na tv ṛṣīṇāṃ manaḥpradoṣān mṛtā ity evaṃ sati kathaṃ tena karmaṇā manodaṇḍaḥ kāyavāgdaṇḍābhyāṃ mahāvadyatamaḥ siddho bhavati | tanmanaḥpradoṣamātreṇa tāvatāṃ sattvānāṃ maraṇāt sidhyati ||
body.translated_text: If it is supposed thus — that the beings dwelling there were destroyed by non-humans (<s>amānuṣa</s>) favorable to them [the sages], and did not die from the ill-will of the sages — then in that case, how is the mind-punishment established through that deed as more greatly faulty than the body-punishment and speech-punishment? It is established precisely because that many beings died from their mere mental ill-will alone.

body.text: yadi vijñaptimātram evedaṃ paracittavidaḥ kiṃ paracittaṃ jānanty atha na | kiṃ cātaḥ | yadi na jānanti kathaṃ paracittavido bhavanti | atha jānanti |
body.translated_text: If everything is <s>vijñaptimātra</s> (consciousness-only), does one who knows others' minds (<s>paracittavid</s>) know others' minds or not? And what follows from this? If he does not know, how are they knowers of others' minds? But if they do know —

children.text:
paracittavidāṃ jñānam ayathārthaṃ kathaṃ yathā |
svacittajñānaṃ
children.translated_text: How is the knowledge of those who know others' minds not in accordance with reality? Just as one's own knowledge of one's own mind

body.text: tad api katham ayathārtha |
body.translated_text: — how is that too not in accordance with reality?

body.text: ajñānād yathā buddhasya gocaraḥ || 21 ||
body.translated_text: Due to ignorance, just as the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s> is. (verse 21)

body.text: yathā tannirabhilāpyenātmanā buddhānāṃ gocaraḥ | tathā tadajñānāt tadubhayaṃ na yathārthaṃ vitathapratibhāsatayā grāhyagrāhakavikalpasyāprahīṇatvāt ||
body.translated_text: Just as with its inexpressible own-nature, it is the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s> — so too, due to ignorance of that, both of those are not in accordance with reality, because of the appearance of what is false, since the conceptual construction of grasped and grasper has not been abandoned.

body.text: anantaviniścayaprabhedāgāmbhīryāyāṃ vijñaptimātratāyāṃ |
body.translated_text: In <s>vijñaptimātratā</s> (consciousness-only), which has infinite distinctions of determinations and unfathomable depth,

children.text:
vijñaptimātratāsiddhiḥ svaśaktisadṛśī mayā |
kṛteyaṃ sarvathā sā tu na cintyā
children.translated_text: this proof of <s>vijñaptimātratā</s> (consciousness-only) has been composed by me in accordance with my own ability. But in its entirety, it is inconceivable —

children.text: Vvs_11

body.text: sarvaprakārā tu sā mādṛśaiś cintayituṃ na śakyate | tarkāviṣayatvāt | kasya punaḥ sā sarvathā gocara ity āha |
body.translated_text: but in all its aspects, it cannot be thought through by ones such as myself, because it is beyond the domain of reasoning. Whose domain then is it in all its aspects? To this he says:

body.text: buddhagocaraḥ || 22 ||
body.translated_text: it is the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>. (verse 22)

body.text: buddhānāṃ hi sā bhagavatāṃ sarvaprakāraṃ gocaraḥ sarvākārasarvajñeyajñānāvighātād iti ||
body.translated_text: For it is the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, in all its aspects, because their knowledge of all knowables in all modes is unobstructed.

body.text:
viṃśatikā vijñaptimātratāsiddhiḥ |
kṛtir iyam ācāryavasubandhoḥ |
body.translated_text: The <s>Viṃśatikā</s> (Twenty Verses), the Proof of Consciousness-Only. This is the work of teacher <s>Vasubandhu</s>.
